newsitem.title: KENYA: Rebels kill 135 people in Burundi- spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Rebels kill 135 people in Burundi- spokesman.

text.p: A spokesman for Burundi's military ruler said on Thursday that Hutu rebels had killed 135 civilians and wounded about 140 by shooting them and slashing them with machetes in northwestern Burundi.

Jean-Luc Ndizeye, military ruler Pierre Buyoya's spokesman, said "terrorists" attacked Buganda commune in Cibitoke province on Wednesday night, apparently after residents refused to cooperate with them.

"They killed 135 people and we also have roughly 140 wounded and 350 burned houses. Some have machete wounds and others were shot. They apparently attacked them because they would not side with them," he said by telephone from Burundi's capital Bujumbura.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report. Cibitoke is one of the most dangerous provinces in Burundi and all foreign aid workers pulled out last year.
"The government is doing all it can to evacuate the wounded to the nearest hospitals," he said. Asked if the army was searching for the attackers, he said the dead were still being counted.
Asked whether survivors said the attack was mounted by Hutu rebels, Ndizeye said: "They are the ones doing this kind of operation. We can see their stamp on it." He gave no details.
Buganda is four km (2.5 miles) from the border with a part of eastern Zaire held since last year by Tutsi-dominated Zairean rebels. The commune is 50 km (30 miles) north of Bujumbura.
The Tutsi-dominated Burundian army said on Tuesday its troops had killed 50 Hutu rebels in fighting south of Bujumbura last Friday and two of its soldiers had been killed.
Army spokesman Isaie Nibizi said the army seized 13 weapons on Friday in Muhuta area, 27 km (17 miles) south of Bujumbura.

More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between Hutu rebels and the Tutsi-dominated army since the killing of Burundi's first freely elected Hutu president in October 1993.
Buyoya, a former military ruler, seized power again in an army coup last July from Burundi's Hutu civilian president.
Regional states imposed sanctions on Burundi shortly after the coup, demanding unconditional talks between the government and rebels led by Hutu guerrilla leader Leonard Nyangoma.
Authorities said last week they had foiled a plot to assassinate Buyoya and arrested eight people including five members of the Parena party, led by former military ruler Jean -Baptiste Bagaza.
Buyoya ousted Bagaza in 1987. Both are Tutsis.
